scope: Anonymous game HTTP and WebSocket surfaces, private room isolation, server-authoritative match inputs and static/private file boundaries
Disabled character-creation and account routes, retained public community catalog and archived published art
Current npm lockfile, the exact deployed container OS and npm packages, manual Node/native runtime inventory and current primary advisories
Read-only inventory of installed Ubuntu package metadata and the shared Caddy binary; isolated patched proxy candidate

resolved.finding: An anonymous private-room ready toggle triggered an identical global lobby broadcast to unrelated guests.
resolved.fix: Skip discovery invalidation for private-only changes and suppress consecutive identical global snapshots. Explicit list requests and public room changes still work.

resolved.finding: Browsers could open guest sockets from an unrelated website; there is no authenticated WebSocket identity to hijack.
resolved.fix: Reject different complete browser origins, using forwarded protocol only across the Express trusted-proxy boundary. Same-site aliases and native guest tooling remain supported.

resolved.classification: known package advisories, not demonstrated remote exploits
resolved.finding: The previous image contained 13 advisory records: 4 HIGH, 8 MEDIUM and 1 LOW. Twelve were in the unused globally bundled npm dependency tree; one was the Alpine zlib package.
resolved.fix: Build the runtime from updated Alpine packages and copy only Node and locked production dependencies. Exclude npm, npx and Yarn from the final image.

fix: Production CSP with fresh per-response nonces and no untrusted inline JavaScript
HSTS on HTTPS, nosniff, frame restrictions, no-referrer for private invitations and browser capability policy preserving fullscreen/gamepad
No-store HTML with matching CSP nonce; immutable fingerprinted asset caching retained
HTTP partial headers and requests close after bounded timeouts, with no limit on total admitted players or rooms
Non-root Node process, read-only root filesystem and bounded /tmp tmpfs
Data volume remains writable for SQLite and retained published content
No Linux capabilities, no privilege escalation, existing memory/CPU/PID constraints retained
Unused provider API key overridden empty while creation remains disabled
CI audits the complete lockfile, scans the exact runtime image and runs the read-only-container HTTP/WebSocket smoke; no advisory ignore file or ignore-unfixed filter is used

validation.admissionStillOpen: The 302-client / 151-match integration test passes beyond the former global ceilings. No new global admission cap was introduced.
validation.reverseProxySpoofedForwardedHeaders: Both public hostnames overwrite spoofed forwarded protocol/host; CSP uses the proper wss authority and HSTS remains active.
validation.ciHostedRun: Workflow commands were exercised locally; no GitHub-hosted run was triggered.

qualityPreserved.browserGame: Actual CPU match rendered on desktop and touch landscape; movement input held/released, ten touch controls and 18 audio resources available, no unexpected CSP violations or JS errors. An intentional script without a nonce was correctly blocked.

openItems.finding: The shared Caddy v2.11.7 binary is compiled with Go 1.26.8 and golang.org/x/net v0.59.0. Current advisories include HTTP Range/HTTP2/TLS availability bugs. Versioning Caddy alone missed these embedded dependency advisories.
openItems.candidate: Caddy v2.11.7 rebuilt with Go 1.26.9 and x/net v0.60.0; module IDs match; configuration, HTTPS, HTTP/2 and WSS tests pass. Candidate has no CVE records and one module-level OpenPGP warning for a package absent from the build graph.
openItems.approvalReason: Replacing the shared proxy process can interrupt other hosted applications.

openItems.finding: The Node project announced security releases for Node 24, 26 and 22 on or shortly after 2026-10-21. The deployed 24.22.0 is the latest Node 24 LTS available on the audit date; migrating to another announced line would not resolve the notice.
openItems.nextStep: Rebuild with the patched Node 24 image when published, repeat the scans/tests/browser smoke and deploy.

openItems.finding: The VM runs kernel 6.17.0-1020-oracle while /boot/vmlinuz points to the installed 7.0.0-1013-oracle. The OS has a reboot-required marker.
openItems.approvalReason: A VM reboot interrupts other services and this T3 environment.

openItems.classification: unverified guest progression; competitive integrity limitation
openItems.finding: Guests can declare 9999 wins in create, join and select without playing previous matches. The server accepts that field for unlocks. An isolated real WebSocket match confirmed advanced combo bonus 7 versus basic bonus 3 for the same input sequence; super unlocks also trust the declared count but still require 75 energy.
openItems.impact: A modified client can claim unlocks early, so the existing casual game does not guarantee verified competitive progression. This does not grant account access or privileged server resources.
openItems.preservedRequirement: Keep existing local/offline progression, gameplay rules and anonymous access. There is no trusted server record from which to authenticate legacy local wins.
openItems.nextStep: Design equal unlock rules for an explicit competitive mode or separate server-verified progression; never use guest-declared wins as verified ranking, prize or authorization data.

openItems.finding: A read-only scan of installed Ubuntu package metadata reports source-package advisory matches, many without vendor fixes. HIGH/CRITICAL matches are limited to kernel-source tool/header packages. These are not confirmed exploitable application findings and are not a scan of the actual running kernel.
openItems.note: Do not interpret raw package-match counts as distinct remote vulnerabilities; no clean-host or zero-CVE-host claim is made.

openItems.finding: Online SQLite plus art backups are verified locally, but recovery after VM/disk deletion still requires an offsite destination.

limits: No security review can establish absence of all vulnerabilities or protection against future CVEs.
Image scanning does not certify the VM, proxy, every native embedded component, or network denial-of-service resistance.
No production fuzzing, exploit attempt, resource exhaustion, credential access, paid API request or test against another hosted app was performed.
Origin checks do not authenticate anonymous users and do not block native bots; public capacity remains finite.
No future patch deployment or recurring monitoring task was scheduled.
